problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=2x-{x}^{2}+3xy,\,y(0)=2
$$

The **implicit** Euler method is applied with step size $Δx=1.$ 
Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and the current value $y.$
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the implicit Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{new}}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =(2{x}_{\text{new}}-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}+3{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}})\cdot 1 \\  & =2{x}_{\text{new}}-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}+3{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy$ and solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+2{x}_{\text{new}}-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}+3{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}}-3{x}_{\text{new}}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+2{x}_{\text{new}}-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2} \\ {y}_{\text{new}}(1-3{x}_{\text{new}}) & =y+2{x}_{\text{new}}-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y+2{x}_{\text{new}}-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}}{1-3{x}_{\text{new}}}\end{aligned}
$$
